fix.notes: The fix is safe for all multi-face layouts: split cards already have `c.name = 'Fire // Ice'` (front+back combined), so their back-face entries like 'Ice' are added only if no standalone 'Ice' card exists. Transform, modal_dfc, and meld cards get their distinct back-face names indexed. The seasons.py set() change is correctness-only with no performance concern.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

When a double-faced card like *The Irencrag // Irencrag* transforms, the bot looks up the back-face name ("Irencrag") to check legality. `oracle.init()` only indexed cards by their front-face name (`c.name`), so "Irencrag" was not found in `CARDS_BY_NAME`, causing the bot to report the card as not legal.

## What changed

**`magic/oracle.py`** — In `init()`, after indexing `CARDS_BY_NAME[c.name] = c`, iterate over `c.names[1:]` (the back-face names stored as a list by `determine_value`) and add each to `CARDS_BY_NAME` only if it is not already a key. This preserves front-face entries and avoids overwriting cards that happen to share a name with a back face.

**`decksite/views/seasons.py`** — The seasons page counts legal cards by iterating `oracle.CARDS_BY_NAME.values()`. With back-face names now also pointing to the same `Card` object, the same card would be counted twice. Changed to `set(oracle.CARDS_BY_NAME.values())`, which deduplicates via `Card.__hash__` (based on `card.name`).

**`magic/oracle_test.py`** — Added two unit tests: one verifying that back-face names are indexed, and one verifying that a back-face name does not override an existing front-face card entry.

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit` — 847 passed, 1 skipped (full unit suite)

Fixes #11992

evidence.detail: CARDS_BY_NAME is populated with canonical name (front face) and flavor_name aliases only — back face names of transform/DFC cards are never added as keys
add_aliases() only adds printed_name when `printed_name != face['name']` for English cards — for English DFCs the back face printed_name equals the face name so no alias is created for the back face

valid_name() searches CARDS_BY_NAME by exact name, then by text before '/', then by canonicalized match — 'Irencrag' (back face) would not match 'The Irencrag' (front face key) under any of these paths, raising InvalidDataException

triage.fix_sketch: In `magic/oracle.py` inside `init()`, after `CARDS_BY_NAME[c.name] = c`, also index back face names from `c.get('names', '').split('|')[1:]` for cards with two faces — only adding a back-face name if it is not already a key in CARDS_BY_NAME (to avoid overriding front-face entries). This makes back-face names resolvable via `valid_name()` so the bot can look up legality for 'Irencrag' (the equipment form). Also update `decksite/views/seasons.py:19` to use `set(oracle.CARDS_BY_NAME.values())` to avoid overcounting newly-indexed back faces. ~10-15 lines total.
